# sq-42 — Publish the null-spelling bounds in limits

`fields[].nullSpellings` and `table.rowClasses.allNullRowSpellings` keep at most 64 distinct spellings of at most 256 characters each (`SpellingCounter.MaxSpellings`, `MaxLength`) and count the rest in `nullSpellingsOther` and `allNullRowSpellingsOther`. Both bounds are internal constants. Publish them in the descriptor's `limits` block and document them in docs/descriptor.md. **Not in this slice:** making the bounds configurable; changing their values; counting the distinct spellings in the "other" counters (the next item).

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

A downstream consumer that must know whether a spelling was dropped has to hard-code 64 and 256 and re-check them on every squalify version bump. sq-36 shipped them as fixed and unpublished, and descriptor.md says so ("these two bounds are fixed, they are not in `limits`"); a consumer that reads `limits` is the one place it already looks for caps (`nullTokens`, `unitTable`, `shapeCharsPerField`, `budget`, the sq-38 sketch levels).

- docs/descriptor.md (the `limits` section, the `nullSpellings` and `allNullRowSpellings` paragraphs that say the bounds are not in `limits`, the consumer subset and versioning policy), design.md, user-guide.md; every golden descriptor if the members are always written
